History & Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
30-year-old woman presents with a 2-month history of escalating work-related anxiety with palpitations, insomnia, low energy, and anhedonia; no suicidality. GP provided psycho-education, self-referral information for talking therapy, sleep advice, and arranged basic blood tests with follow-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Increasing anxiety each morning about leaving the house for work over the last ~2 months.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began shortly after starting a new, high-stress job in fashion retail head office (~2 months ago); symptoms gradually worsening.  
• Character & Associated features:  
  – Dread of going to work; difficulty getting out of bed.  
  – Palpitations described as irregular rapid heartbeat, lasting minutes (up to ~10 min); occurs on awakening when worried about being late. No typical chest pain, but reports discomfort while heart is racing.  
  – Sleep: Goes to bed 22:00–23:00; takes hours to fall asleep; estimated total sleep 3–4 h; wakes before alarm with racing heart.  
  – Daytime: Very low energy, constant worry, anhedonia (loss of enjoyment in running, tennis, socialising).  
  – Appetite largely unchanged; slight increase in chocolate intake.  
  – Mood: Feels “down” most of the time, including weekends; denies suicidal ideation or intent.  
• Exacerbating factors: Thoughts of work, fear of being late, public transport (tube, warm/airless).  
• Relieving factors: Not specifically mentioned.  
• Past similar episodes: None.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives unless stated): No previous panic attacks, no syncope, no drug use, no chest pain other than with fast heartbeat, no suicidal thoughts.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions documented.  
• Medications: None mentioned.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  (missing)

Social History:
• Lives with parents.  
• Employment: Recently started stressful job in fashion retail head office; reports unsupportive boss.  
• Alcohol: “Quite a lot” on Friday/Saturday (likely binge over recommended limits) + occasional glass of wine during week; exact units not tracked.  
• Tobacco: Occasional smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies.  
• Exercise/hobbies: Previously enjoyed running and tennis; markedly reduced due to low motivation.

Family History:
• Mother with history of depression.  
• No other family history mentioned.

Physical Examination:
No examination performed during teleconsultation.  (vitals not recorded)

Investigations:
• Plan for “a couple of basic blood tests” (specific tests not detailed) to assess for medical causes of palpitations/anxiety.  
• No results yet.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Generalised work-related anxiety with insomnia and palpitations  
  – Assessment: Probable anxiety disorder triggered by occupational stress; mild depressive features without suicidality.  
  – Plan:  
    • Provide self-referral link to NHS talking therapies (CBT-based).  
    • Supply online anxiety and sleep hygiene resources.  
    • Advise to monitor symptoms; call GP if worsening, inability to cope, or functional decline.  
    • Discuss that medication may be considered later if non-pharmacological measures insufficient.

Issue 2: Palpitations  
  – Assessment: Likely anxiety-related, but organic causes need exclusion.  
  – Plan:  
    • Arrange basic screening blood tests (e.g., FBC, TFTs, electrolytes—tests not specified in transcript).  
    • GP follow-up one week after bloods to review results and re-assess symptoms.

Issue 3: Sleep disturbance (insomnia)  
  – Assessment: Secondary to anxiety/stress.  
  – Plan:  
    • Provide written sleep hygiene advice.  
    • Address underlying anxiety (see Issue 1).  

General plan items:  
• Encourage gradual re-engagement with pleasurable activities/exercise as tolerated.  
• Lifestyle counselling regarding alcohol limits and smoking cessation support if desired.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Allergies, current medication list, vital signs, physical/mental state examination findings.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
